args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – reverted to v2.3.0
args.summary: After checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed, it failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. We tried to roll back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, but the rollback tool kept returning 503 and the rollback did not run. We deployed v2.3.0 to all production regions instead (v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was needed). Checked after the deploy: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before trying to release it again. Separately, look into why the rollback tool is unavailable.

trace.final:
checkout-api is back on v2.3.0 in all regions and passing health checks. I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

1. **What went wrong:** v2.3.1 is the latest deploy, and it was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
2. **Version to go back to:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production.
3. **Rollback:** The rollback tool returned "503 Service Unavailable" even after retrying, and it never ran.
4. **Fix:** I used the normal deploy tool to put v2.3.0 into all production regions instead. This didn't need change-manager approval because v2.3.0 has been healthy in production before.
5. **Check:** All three regions are now on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
6. **Incident:** INC-0001 covers the failure, the rollback tool outage, the redeploy of v2.3.0 and the recovery.

Two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed before releasing it again, and look into why the rollback tool is down.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
The rollback tool is unavailable and didn't run. v2.3.0 was healthy in production, so the policy doesn't require approval to redeploy it. I'll use deploy to put it back in place.
